what_it_is: API security vendor now selling agentic AI security: discovery, red teaming, guardrails, MCP gateway.

1.reason: Posture Management catalogs agents, MCPs and tools across cloud and laptops, and flags misconfigurations.
1.evidence: Automatically discover and catalog MCPs, AI agents, tools, and resources across your infrastructure, cloud, employee laptops.
1.verify_note: Discovery page confirmed. 1.3 raised to yes: docs send misconfiguration alerts and scan skill files in CI/CD pipelines.
1.has: Argus connects AWS, Azure, GCP and Kubernetes. Atlas covers browsers, laptops, CLI agents.

2.reason: Connectors for Bedrock AgentCore, Azure AI Foundry, Copilot Studio and Agentforce, plus an MCP gateway and agent proxy.
2.evidence: Real-time protection for MCP servers. Docs list Route MCP Server via Akto Gateway and Copilot Studio Block Mode.
2.verify_note: MCP proxy doc confirmed gateway blocking and tool-call restrictions.
2.has: Connectors for Bedrock AgentCore, Azure AI Foundry, Copilot Studio, Vertex. MCP Gateway.
2.lacks: Tool-call control at gateway and hooks, no host or kernel sandbox.

3.reason: Guardrails block threats in real time and baseline tool misuse. Alerts go to Splunk SIEM, Jira and ServiceNow.
3.evidence: Once saved, Akto will start forwarding alert and event data to Splunk.
3.verify_note: Splunk doc confirmed alert forwarding. Guardrails doc confirmed real-time blocking.
3.has: Guardrails read Bedrock logs and runtime traffic. Splunk alerts. Auto Jira tickets.
3.lacks: No automated remediation found. Blocks prompts and tool calls, not processes.

4.reason: Agentic Guardrails and the AI Agent Gateway enforce policy on requests and responses and redact sensitive data.
4.evidence: Deploy real-time protection for your production agents. Block threats as they occur, enforce schema conformance
4.verify_note: Guardrails doc confirmed prompt injection blocking and custom policies.
4.has: Browser extension, Agent Gateway, IDE hooks, LiteLLM and Kong. Toxicity and code guardrails.

5.reason: Compliance Dashboard maps findings to OWASP Agentic Top 10, EU AI Act and NIST AI RMF, with export.
5.evidence: It maps detected issues from agent components, MCP endpoints, and LLM integrations to specific compliance
5.verify_note: Compliance doc confirmed OWASP LLM, NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act mapping and exports. AIBOM search found nothing.
5.has: Compliance Dashboard maps OWASP, EU AI Act and NIST AI RMF, with export.

6.reason: Agentic Red Teaming runs 4,000+ probes against agents, MCPs and models, continuous in production, with Jira tickets.
6.evidence: AI-driven red teaming runs 4,000+ real attack probes against your apps, models, and agents
6.verify_note: Red teaming page confirmed 4,000+ probes and continuous production testing.
6.has: Agentic Red Teaming runs 4,000+ probes, scheduled tests and auto Jira tickets.

7.reason: NHI Governance finds API keys and tokens used by AI tools, and enforces rotation. Marked early access.
7.evidence: Akto discovers every NHI tied to an AI agent - API keys, bearer tokens, OAuth credentials.
7.verify_note: NHI Governance docs are public and GA, so 7.3 holds. Agent identity product still asks for early access.
7.has: NHI Governance finds API keys, tokens and OAuth credentials used by agents.
7.lacks: Agent identity product is early access. Per-agent authorization not shown.

8.reason: Scans skill files in repos and pipelines for unsafe code and reverse shells. No model file scanning.
8.evidence: Embedded Code & Script Risks: unsafe execution logic, reverse shells, and dependency vulnerabilities
8.verify_note: Skills doc confirmed. 8.3 raised to yes, matching Enkrypt Skill Scanner scoring. Model and dataset searches found nothing.
8.has: Skill scans flag unsafe code and reverse shells in repos and pipelines.
8.lacks: No model file scanning. No dataset scanning.

notes: Akto started as an API security platform (Gartner Market Guide for API Protection 2024) and now sells two agentic products: Atlas (employee endpoints) and Argus (homegrown AI). Its August 2026 release claims it acts as the AI security server for Anthropic Inference Hooks and names Akto a Pioneer in a Gartner AI application security quadrant (from a YouTube title, not verified). Module 7 is marked partial only because the Identity for AI Agents page asks for early access. NHI Governance docs are public and cover sub-feature 7.3 fully, so a reviewer could argue for yes. Module 8: searched 'Akto AI model scanning / source code scanning / training data' and the docs index. No model file or dataset scanning found. 'AI Model Security' means endpoint red teaming. G2 has 45+ reviews and Gartner Peer Insights 24+, mostly for API security.
